scenes.title: NVG How-To
scenes.text: How to put on night vision goggles. This video shows how to mount the AN/PVS-14 on your helmet and check the mount, what night vision does to your eyes, the principles of night vision from TC 21-305-2, and ends with a knowledge check.

scenes.title: Why Night Vision
scenes.text: Night vision lets you see and drive without white light. You can spot terrain, obstacles, and people in near darkness, keep light discipline, and see infrared markers and signals. Because the PVS-14 is a monocular, your other eye stays free for the mirrors, the instruments, and as a backup.

scenes.title: Know the Equipment
scenes.text: Know the parts. The helmet carries a front bracket, called the shroud. The helmet mount locks into the shroud, and the PVS-14 locks into the mount. A lanyard ties the device to the helmet, and a counterweight on the back balances the load.

scenes.title: Inspect Before You Mount
scenes.text: Do inspect everything first. Check the shroud screws are tight and the shroud is not cracked. Check the mount for cracks, bent parts, and worn locking points, and make sure every adjustment knob moves and locks. Then run PMCS on the PVS-14 itself. Turn in any damaged part. Don't tape it or improvise a fix.

scenes.title: Attach the Mount
scenes.text: Attach the mount to the shroud. Line it up, push it in until it locks, and listen for the click. Then pull on it firmly. If it moves or comes out, it is not locked. Check it again every time the helmet comes off and goes back on.

scenes.title: Attach the PVS-14
scenes.text: Next, slide the PVS-14 into the mount until it locks, and pull test it the same way. Attach the lanyard every time, so a dropped device hangs from your helmet instead of hitting the ground. Make sure the battery cap is tight before you go.

scenes.title: Fit the Helmet
scenes.text: Put the helmet on and tighten the chin strap and the retention system. A loose helmet means a moving image. Add the counterweight if one is issued, so the helmet does not tip forward. Push the helmet by hand. It should not slide on your head.

scenes.title: Adjust the Position
scenes.text: Lower the device in front of your eye. Use the eye your training or unit SOP specifies, usually your dominant eye. Adjust the height, then slide it in or out until you see the full circle, without the eyecup pressing on your eye. Tilt it so the image is level.

scenes.title: Power On and Focus
scenes.text: Turn the device on in the dark, or with the daylight cover in place. Focus the eyepiece diopter first, until the image noise is sharp, then focus the objective lens on something at driving distance. If you wear glasses or issued inserts, focus with them on.

scenes.title: Do the Shake Test
scenes.text: Now do the shake test. Nod and turn your head firmly. The image should stay steady and the device should not sag or shift. If it moves, take it off, find the problem, and fix it before you drive.

scenes.title: Drive With a Loose Mount
scenes.text: Don't drive with a loose mount. A sagging device bounces the image, pulls your attention off the road, and strains your neck. A device that falls can hit your face or eye, and a lost sensitive item stops the mission.

scenes.title: Stow and Remove
scenes.text: To stow, flip the device up and turn it off. To remove it, unlock it from the mount, put the lens caps on, and take out the battery for storage. Account for the device, and turn it in according to your unit SOP. Never carry the helmet by the mount or the device.

scenes.title: What NVGs Do to Your Eyes
scenes.text: Here is what night vision does to your eyes. Long use causes eye strain, fatigue, and headaches. You see less detail and poor depth through the tube. Your two eyes see different images, which takes effort. After you take the device off, colors may look shifted for a short time, and the aided eye needs time to adjust to the dark. These effects are normally temporary.

scenes.title: Protect Your Eyes
scenes.text: Do protect your eyes. Take breaks, and follow the rest plan. Keep the eyecup clean, and clean it before sharing a device. Never look at a laser, with or without night vision. If you have eye pain, blurred vision, or headaches that do not go away, report it to medical.

scenes.title: Vision Is Your Key Sense
scenes.text: Now, the principles of night vision. Vision is the most important sense you use while driving. You need good depth perception for judging height and distance, good night vision techniques for efficiency in night operations, and good visual acuity for identifying terrain features and obstacles.

scenes.title: How the Eye Works
scenes.text: Here is how the eye works. The cornea is the clear, protective front of the eye. Light enters through the pupil, and the iris, the colored part of the eye, controls how much light gets in. The lens focuses the light on the retina, the lining at the back of the eye where the image is formed. That image is upside down, and the brain turns it right way up.

scenes.title: Acuity and Types of Vision
scenes.text: Visual acuity is the accuracy of how well you see, measured for each eye with a standard eye chart. Photopic vision works in daylight. Scotopic vision works in darkness. Mesopic vision is used at dawn, at dusk, and during other mid-light levels.

scenes.title: Dark Adaptation and Flash Protection
scenes.text: Maximum dark adaptation is reached in about thirty to forty-five minutes. If you expect a flash or high-intensity light from a known direction, turn the vehicle away from it. If you don't know the direction, close one eye. Once the light is no longer a problem, the eye you closed still has enough night vision to keep driving.

scenes.title: What Robs Night Vision
scenes.text: Night myopia blurs vision at night, but special lenses can be prescribed for it. Night driving is more tiring and stressful than day driving. Self-imposed stresses also hurt you. Smoking alone reduces night vision by about twenty percent.

scenes.title: Scanning and Depth Perception
scenes.text: To identify objects, scan from right to left, or left to right, using a slow, regular movement. Depth perception tells you exactly where things are in space. It is what gave our tree-dwelling ancestors their edge as they swung from branch to branch.

scenes.title: Light and Weather
scenes.text: The moon provides the greatest source of ambient light at night. Cloud cover over the moon and stars, along with dew, smoke, and haze, are weather conditions that reduce illumination. Check them before every night mission.

scenes.title: Knowledge Check
scenes.text: Knowledge check. These fourteen questions come from TC 21-305-2, quiz seven twenty-one, five hundred, oh one point five, Principles of Night Vision. Answer each one before the answer appears, and pause the video if you need more time.

scenes.title: Question 1 of 14
scenes.q: Vision is the most important sense you use while driving. You need good ____ for determining height and distance, good ____ for efficiency in night operations, and good ____ for identifying terrain features and obstacles.
scenes.text: Question one: you need good what for height and distance, good what for efficiency at night, and good what for identifying terrain? Answer: depth perception, night vision techniques, and visual acuity.

scenes.title: Question 2 of 14
scenes.q:
Identify the portions of the eye that correspond to the following descriptions:
____ Clear, protective part of the eye.
____ The lining at the back of the eye where the image is formed.
____ The colored portion of the eye.
scenes.text: Question two: name the clear protective part of the eye, the lining where the image is formed, and the colored portion. Answer: cornea, retina, and iris.

scenes.title: Question 3 of 14
scenes.q: Light enters your eye through the ____. The amount of light entering the eye is controlled by the ____. The light passes through the ____ which focuses it on the ____ at the back of the eye. The picture seen is upside down, which the ____ turns right way up.
scenes.text: Question three: fill in the path of light, from where it enters the eye, to what turns the picture right way up. Answer: pupil, iris, lens, retina, and brain.

scenes.title: Question 4 of 14
scenes.q: The accuracy of how well you see is known as ____. It is determined for each eye by reading a standard eye chart.
scenes.text: Question four: the accuracy of how well you see is known as what? Answer: B, visual acuity.

scenes.title: Question 5 of 14
scenes.q: What type of vision is used at dawn, at dusk, and during periods of mid-light levels?
scenes.text: Question five: what type of vision is used at dawn, at dusk, and at mid-light levels? Answer: A, mesopic.

scenes.title: Question 6 of 14
scenes.q: Night myopia is a visual problem that affects night vision. A person with this condition will experience blurred vision at night. Special lenses cannot be prescribed for this condition.
scenes.text: Question six, true or false: special lenses cannot be prescribed for night myopia. Answer: false. Special lenses can be prescribed.

scenes.title: Question 7 of 14
scenes.q: Maximum dark adaptation is reached in about ____.
scenes.text: Question seven: maximum dark adaptation is reached in about how long? Answer: A, thirty to forty-five minutes.

scenes.title: Question 8 of 14
scenes.q: If a flash or high intensity light is expected from a specific direction, turn the vehicle away from the light source. If the direction is not known, close one eye. Once the light source is no longer a problem, the eye that was closed will provide enough night vision to continue driving.
scenes.text: Question eight, true or false: closing one eye protects enough night vision to keep driving after a flash. Answer: true.

scenes.title: Question 9 of 14
scenes.q: Night driving is more tiring and stressful than day driving.
scenes.text: Question nine, true or false: night driving is more tiring and stressful than day driving. Answer: true.

scenes.title: Question 10 of 14
scenes.q: Of the following self-imposed stresses, ____ reduces 20 percent of a person's night vision.
scenes.text: Question ten: which self-imposed stress reduces night vision by twenty percent? Answer: B, smoking.

scenes.title: Question 11 of 14
scenes.q: Night vision scanning techniques are important in object identification. Select the statement that best describes the proper scanning technique.
choices: a. Scan from right to left, or left to right, using a slow, regular movement.
b. Scan from up to down, or down to up, using a regular movement.
c. Rapidly scan the horizon from right to left or left to right.
scenes.text: Question eleven: which statement best describes the proper scanning technique? Answer: A, right to left or left to right, using a slow, regular movement.

scenes.title: Question 12 of 14
scenes.q: ____ gave our tree-dwelling forefathers an edge when they swung from branch to branch. They knew exactly where in space that next branch was located.
scenes.text: Question twelve: what gave our tree-dwelling forefathers their edge, swinging from branch to branch? Answer: A, depth perception.

scenes.title: Question 13 of 14
scenes.q: The ____ provides the greatest source of ambient light at night.
scenes.text: Question thirteen: what provides the greatest source of ambient light at night? Answer: B, the moon.

scenes.title: Question 14 of 14
scenes.q: Cloud coverage of the moon and stars, ____ are examples of weather considerations that reduce illumination.
choices: c. Dust, smoke, haze, dew, and lightning.
scenes.text: Question fourteen: along with cloud cover, which weather conditions reduce illumination? Answer: B, dew, smoke, and haze.

scenes.title: Recap
scenes.text: To recap. Inspect the shroud and mount, lock in the mount and the device, and pull test both. Attach the lanyard, tighten the helmet, and add the counterweight. Adjust and focus, do the shake test, and never drive with a loose mount. Protect your eyes, know the principles of night vision, and stow and account for the device.

scenes.title: See the Night
scenes.text: Mount it right, and the night is yours. Verify these steps against the AN/PVS-14 and helmet mount operator manuals, TC 21-305-2, and your unit SOP.
